title: Multi-process payment webhook on SQLite: fulfill each paid order exactly once, across restarts
contract: One paid order leads to exactly one fulfillment, even when the webhook is delivered concurrently to several worker processes sharing one SQLite database, redelivered after a process restart, or sent under a different event ID; a failed fulfillment is never marked complete and can be retried by another process.
language: javascript (ESM, Node 24, built-ins only incl. node:sqlite)
interface: export async function handleWebhook(event, deps) -> Promise<{ ok: boolean, action: "fulfilled" | "duplicate" | "ignored" }>; deps = { db: DatabaseSync from node:sqlite, open on a database file shared by several worker processes (journal_mode=WAL, busy_timeout=5000 already set; the handler owns its schema), fulfillOrder: async (orderId: string) => void (may throw) }; each worker process imports handler.mjs fresh, so module memory is not shared across processes or restarts

cases.title: 20 deliveries across 4 concurrent worker processes fulfill the order once
Redelivery after a process restart (same and different event ID) does not fulfill again
Unknown and non-paid event types are acknowledged and ignored
Two different orders delivered from 2 processes are each fulfilled exactly once
Failed fulfillment is not marked complete; a new process retries it exactly once
Module exports handleWebhook, fulfills a valid event and persists state in deps.db

scope: Verified for these synthetic conditions in this sandbox (separate worker processes sharing one SQLite file per case). Not a production guarantee.
